findings.summary: The extractive logic of competence, which is what the scene is about, was removed.

evidence.baseline: This is the extractive logic of competence, and it is exactly the sentiment the rotation requirement exists to override. The architecture does not rotate Mahlinah out because Mahlinah has failed. It rotates Mahlinah out because a community that allows its best steward to hold a constitutional role indefinitely is a community that is, slowly and with the best intentions, building a dependency that will eventually become a vulnerability.

findings.diagnosis: The extractive logic of competence names a pressure the volume has no other term for, and the not because she failed construction is what keeps the rotation from reading as a demotion. Slowly and with the best intentions is the same structural rather than moral move the whole volume makes, dramatized in one person.

findings.summary: The scene's argument about what the awkwardness costs and buys was removed.

evidence.baseline: The awkwardness is the point. The architecture does not produce a smooth transfer of competence. It produces a real one, in which the community accepts a temporary decline in the quality of facilitation as the price of not building a dependency on a single irreplaceable person. A community optimizing for short-term operational excellence would never make this trade.

findings.diagnosis: The card protects the sentence about Mahlinah and Elan's awkward handoff. The protected line survived in the shipped text and the paragraph that explains what the awkwardness is buying did not, which is the volume's recurring pattern. The trade is the payoff of the time architecture chapter, named explicitly.

openQuestions: The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the scene keeps both the extractive logic of competence and the committing constitutional claim that the architecture does not bend to individual excellence; the awkwardness trade keeps both its cost and its purchase. R-PAIRED-DELETION: Mahlinah, Elan, relational stewardship, and the mentorship function were swept; the Tuesday and water sections carry the other ends and all stand. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: the card-protected line re-verified at width: The meeting is awkward because Elan is still learning and both of them know it replaces the baseline's slightly awkward and not yet good at the role as the paragraph's landing, exactly as the original kept note records, and nothing beyond the protected line moved. R-VOICE-BIND holds the protected form against the baseline. R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY: nothing else seeded; CTD-0030 re-verified, the scene stays inside the design fiction frame. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: the protected line is card-held, not merit-kept, so no credit attaches, stated explicitly. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Fourteen of eighteen baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the four glyph repairs and the card-protected landing, all attributed. No prose change required.
corrections: The original itemization is corrected: four em dash glyphs, the stewardship pair standing as a comma pair and the single dashes at individual excellence and the mentorship function standing as commas, with the comma before and the meeting becoming a period so the protected line lands as its own sentence.
